orientation.batter_faces: EAST to EAST-SOUTHEAST. The batter at home plate looks out over the diamond toward centre field to the east / east-southeast; McCovey Cove and the Bay lie beyond right field to the south-east/south, and the left-field/centre-field bleachers face back toward the city skyline. The sun rises over the left-field / centre-field wall, tracks around the right-field foul pole around midday, moves behind the first-base stands in the afternoon, and sets behind home plate and the third-base grandstand. Consequently the FIRST-BASE side is the shade side and the THIRD-BASE line and the outfield are the sunny side.

numbering_direction.summary: SECTION NUMBERS INCREASE FROM THE FIRST-BASE / RIGHT-FIELD-CORNER SIDE TOWARD THE THIRD-BASE / LEFT-FIELD SIDE, i.e. they increase TOWARD THIRD BASE. LOW numbers = first base line and the right-field corner. HIGH numbers = third base line, then left field. Every one of the three numbered series (100s, 200s, 300s) runs the SAME way; none is reversed. IMPORTANT SPECIAL CASE - THE 100 SERIES IS A FULL LOOP: it starts at 101 in the right-field corner / far end of the first base line, runs up the first-base line to home plate, continues down the third-base line to the left-field corner at 135, then keeps going around the OUTFIELD - bleachers 136-144 across left field, left-centre and centre field - and finally comes back to the Arcade on top of the RIGHT FIELD wall at 145-152, closing the circle next to 101. So the HIGHEST 100-level numbers (145-152) are in RIGHT FIELD, not left field. Do not read '145-152 are in right field' as evidence that numbering runs the other way. PER-SERIES DETAIL: (a) PROMENADE / 100 LEVEL (Lower Box + Field Club + Bleachers + Arcade): 101-107 down the first base line (101 furthest from home) -> 107-109 near the visiting-team dugout -> 110-121 between the dugouts -> 112-119 the home-plate arc (Audi Dugout Club in AAA-DDD rows of 112, 113, 115, 117, 119, 121) -> 121-124 behind the Giants dugout, third base side -> 125-135 down the third base line (132-134 in the left-field corner, 135 in the left-field corner) -> 136-141 left and left-centre field bleachers -> 142-144 centre field bleachers (144 under the scoreboard) -> 145-152 Outfield Arcade on top of the RIGHT FIELD wall over McCovey Cove. Note 111 has no RateYourSeats page and 120 does not appear on any source. (b) CLUB / 200 LEVEL: 202-234, foul pole to foul pole only (does not wrap the outfield). 202-204 are past the right-field end of the playing field ('The view from sections 202-204 is outside of the playing field'); 204-214 are 'on the first base side'; 217 is flagged 'Home Plate View'; 228-230 are 'down the left field line' at the Alaska Airlines Flight Deck; 234 is the high/left-field end. (c) VIEW / 300 LEVEL: 302-336, foul pole to foul pole only. 302 is the right-field corner ('View from Section 302 shows the right field corner sections remaining in the sun the longest'); 313-318 are 'located behind home plate'; 332-336 are 'in left field' and 335-336 are 'near the left field foul pole'. Sections 301, 303, 306, 309, 316, 322 and 329 do not exist in the index. ALL THREE SERIES THEREFORE AGREE: low = first base / right-field corner, high = third base / left field.

Giants official press release, 12 December 2019: 'In a move designed to increase player safety and enhance fan engagement, the San Francisco Giants unveiled designs today for the new bullpens at Oracle Park that will be located behind the centerfield wall in 2020.' with the bullet points 'The new Giants' and visitors' bullpens will be located on either side of The Garden at Oracle Park, just below the left field and centerfield bleachers.' / 'Several bleacher seats will directly overlook the bullpens and two new standing room terraces will be built into the bleachers to enhance fan engagement.' / 'A portion of the Giants' bullpen will be incorporated into The Garden at Oracle Park and fans will now have direct views from The Garden into the Giants' bullpen.' / 'The bullpens will be situated just inches above the field and will be accessible through gates built into the outfield wall.' / 'Padded chain link openings in the wall will provide views into and out of the bullpens for players and fans.' / 'Terraces adjacent to the bullpens will be approximately 3 feet above the bullpens and will offer fans direct views into the bullpens and of the playing field beyond.' / 'The new centerfield wall be shortened from 8' to 7' in height.' / 'Both bullpens will feature bathrooms for players.' (https://www.mlb.com/press-release/press-release-giants-unveil-designs-for-relocated-bullpens ; same text at https://www.mlb.com/giants/fans/construction/bullpens). MLB.com: 'The Giants announced new dimensions for Oracle Park's outfield on Thursday as part of their plan to revamp the park for the 2020 season, which includes relocating the bullpens from foul territory to their new home behind the center-field wall.' and 'The bullpens, which had been located in foul territory since the stadium first opened in 2000, will be placed to the left and right of The Garden at Oracle Park.' and 'two new standing room terraces will be constructed next to the bleachers in left- and right-center field' (https://www.mlb.com/news/giants-to-move-in-outfield-fences-in-2020). WHICH IS WHICH: NBC Sports Bay Area (Alex Pavlovic, 30 June 2020), on the completed pens: 'The bullpen closer to Triples Alley will be for visitors and the one closer to left field is for the Giants. There's an open area for the batting cage in the middle, which is rolled out behind the plate every afternoon for BP.' (https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/mlb/check-out-first-look-at-giants-new-completed-bullpens-at-oracle-park/1288731/). Triples Alley is right-centre field (the Giants A-Z guide lists '- Right Center Field 415 feet (triples alley)'), so the VISITORS' bullpen is on the right-centre side and the GIANTS' bullpen on the left-centre/left side, with the batting cage between them. Ballparks of Baseball: 'That same year, the team announced plans to relocate the bullpens from foul territory to behind the centerfield fence, reducing the outfield dimensions.' Wikipedia: 'The bullpens were moved from foul territory into center field, so the Giants decided to make their garden smaller to fit the bullpens behind the center-field wall.' and gives the motivation 'to address player safety issues that had arisen over the years by having the bullpen mounds in the field of play'. Clem's Baseball: 'Prior to the 2020 season, the bullpens were moved from foul territory to a much safer area beyond the center field fence, which was moved in about eight feet.' The Giants A-Z guide still lists 'Field Level: Performance Center, Home Bullpen, Visitors Bullpen, Engineering Offices'. STALE TEXT TO IGNORE (recorded so downstream stages do not re-import it): a RateYourSeats fan-feedback note on the Section 128 page still says 'The Giants Bullpen is on the Field in Front of Sections 126-128' and a Section 128 Row 3 review says 'Field level seats, right at Giants bullpen area... Right in the middle of the Giants bullpen' - both describe the PRE-2020 foul-territory bullpen on the third-base side. The Giants' own A-Z guide likewise still describes the Jim Beam BaselineBox as 'adjacent to the visitor's bullpen, directly in front of Sections 105 and 106', which describes the PRE-2020 visitors' bullpen in first-base foul territory. Neither reflects the current arrangement.

accessibility.summary: Official source is the Giants' Accessible Services page at https://www.mlb.com/giants/ballpark/accessible-services (plus the A-Z guide at https://www.mlb.com/giants/ballpark/information/guide). VERBATIM key statements: ELEVATORS/RAMPS - 'Elevators are available at Willie Mays Plaza and 2nd & King (below the clock towers) and provide access to all levels of the ballpark. The elevators at Lefty O'Doul and Seals Plaza provide access to the Promenade Level only.' and 'Ramps that provide access to all levels of the ballpark are located at the Willie Mays and 2nd & King Street gates.' The A-Z guide adds: 'In addition, at Willie Mays Plaza there are three escalators, which move guests up before and during the game and change direction after the sixth inning to bring guests down after the game.' GATES - 'There are four main entrances at Oracle Park, all of which offer either an elevator or ramp.' with 'Willie Mays Gate (Third & King streets) - Elevator, ramp and escalators available providing access to all levels of the ballpark'; 'Lefty O'Doul Gate (near the Lefty O'Doul Bridge at Third & Berry streets) - Elevator providing access to the Promenade Level only'; 'Marina Gate (along the Portwalk behind center field) - Elevator providing access to the Promenade Level only'; 'Second & King Street Gate - Elevator, ramp and escalators available providing access to all levels of the ballpark'. LEVEL ACCESS RULES - 'Blue Shield Field Club (Level 1): Accessible to guests with a game ticket for the following seating categories: Blue Shield Field Club, Audi Dugout Club, Batter's Box, Dugout Box.' / 'Promenade Level (Level 2 - Main Concourse): Accessible to all guests with a game ticket.' / 'Club Level (Level 3): Accessible to guests with a game ticket for the following seating categories: Club Level, Blue Shield Field Club, The Loft at McCovey Cove, ElevenLabs Champions Suite, Audi Dugout Club, Batter's Box, Legends Club, Dugout Box, Press Club, Promenade Patio Tables and Airwallex Suite Level.' / 'Airwallex Suite Level (Level 4): Accessible to guests with a ticket for the Airwallex Suite Level, Cloud Club, or Gotham Club.' / 'View Level (Level 5): Accessible to all guests with a game ticket.' RESTROOMS - 'All restrooms in Oracle Park are fully accessible for guests with disabilities.' SHADE ADVICE - 'While shade cannot be guaranteed, we encourage those attempting to purchase seats to target these suggested sections: Lower Box sections rows 30+, Club Level ADA, or furthest back.' NOTE the phrase 'Club Level ADA' and 'furthest back' - the Giants' accessible seating is generally at the BACK of sections. GUEST SERVICES - 'Guest Services personnel are available at the Guest Services Desk, located behind home plate on the Promenade Level, for wheelchair requests, lost and found items... Concierge personnel are available to assist guests on the Club and Oracle Suite levels, near the Willie Mays elevators.' and 'Wheelchairs can be stored free of charge at the Guest Services Desk, located behind home plate on the Promenade Level. Available on a first-come, first-served basis. Guests may also check in with the nearest aisle attendant for storage options closer to your section.' ASSISTIVE LISTENING - 'Assistive listening devices are available at no charge upon request at the Guest Services Station located on the Promenade Level behind home plate near section 119.' TICKETS - 'For events sold through Ticketmaster, the Giants/Oracle Park do not sell or service tickets... Same-day ADA relocations and assistance will be available at Ticket Services inside the ballpark, located behind home plate on the Promenade Level near section 119.' CONTACT - customerservice@sfgiants.com or (415) 972-2209. BOX OFFICE - 'Windows 1-3 at the main Oracle Park box office (on King Street, adjacent to Willie Mays Plaza) are accessible.' CAPTIONING - 'The Giants provide open captioning for all ballpark public address content on the dedicated captioning board located immediately below the DiamondVision display in left-centerfield.' A third-party summary of the Giants' page also states that 'there are accessible rows at the top of most sections within the venue' - consistent with the RateYourSeats Q&A for Section 118 ('Row 42 will be the very last row of seating in Section 118, furthest from the field and closest to the section entry tunnel at the very top of the section. These seats are normally reserved for handicap accessible seating.') - but the exact wording could not be re-verified verbatim on mlb.com, so treat it as MEDIUM confidence.

(b) 100 LEVEL 'BACK-ONLY' SECTIONS behind home plate (no Field Club rows at all): Section 114 - 'Rows in Section 114 are labeled 23-31', entrance at Row 31. Section 132 - 'Rows in Section 132 are labeled 12-41', entrance at Row 41 (the section 'begins behind sections 131 and 135' so it has no low rows at all). seat1_side_verbatim: RateYourSeats states, IDENTICALLY on every Oracle Park section page checked: "When looking towards the field/field/stage, lower number seats are on the right". (Note the doubled word 'field/field/stage' - that is exactly how it renders on the site.) Verified verbatim on these 24 section pages: 101, 107, 112, 113, 114, 115, 116, 117, 118, 119, 121, 123, 128, 132, 136, 145, 152, 202, 217, 234, 302, 313, 318, 336 - i.e. in the right-field corner (101), on the first-base side (107, 112), behind home plate (114-119, 217, 313, 318), on the third-base side (121, 123), in the left-field corner (128, 132), in the left-field bleachers (136), in the right-field Arcade (145, 152), at the right-field ends of the club and view decks (202, 302) and at the left-field ends (234, 336). There is NO variation anywhere: RateYourSeats treats Oracle Park seat numbering as running uniformly RIGHT-to-LEFT as the fan faces the field (seat 1 on the fan's right). NOTE this is the OPPOSITE of the sentence RateYourSeats prints at Citi Field ('lower number seats are on the left'), so the sentence is park-specific, not a site-wide template. CORROBORATION (two independent RateYourSeats Q&A answers, not the boilerplate): Section 112 - 'Row AAA is the first row in this section, while seat 1 will be on the right aisle (closer to section 110).' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/oracle-park/seating/sections/112). Section 302 - 'Seat 1 will be furthest to the right as you face the field from View Reserve Section 302, but the entry into the row will be located on the left side of the section. Therefore, sitting in Seat 1 will require to furthest walk from the aisle to get to the seats in any row in this section.' and 'Section 302 Row 1 specifically has 11 seats in the row, with Seat 11 being on the aisle and Seat 1 being furthest from the aisle.'
